content.thinking:
I'm planning out the wolf's proportions and skeleton structure in detail, defining the hip, spine, and body joint positions needed before writing the full file in one careful pass.

For front legs I'll use a three-name chain (shoulder, elbow, wrist) matching two spans plus a tip, and for hind legs a four-name chain (hip, knee, hock, foot) for three spans plus tip. Paws get small sphere radii around 0.05 with target y near 0.045 so they sit just touching the floor.

Paw spheres are scaled anisotropically and positioned so their bottoms rest at y=0, and the leg sweeps taper down to meet the ankle with rounded caps that keep everything flush with the ground. For the body I'm considering using a single spine chain running from hips through the neck to the head as a loft path.

Now I'm defining the skeleton hierarchy: a spine chain rising from the hips through four points, with hips as the root joint and the spine chain parented to it; the tail and hind legs also parent to hips, while the front legs parent to the last spine joint. I'm sketching a neck chain of a few points leading up to a head joint, deciding whether to add a third neck point to give it a proper tip segment.

For the body loft, I'm working out which joints should influence the mesh shape, considering whether to include just the spine or both hips and spine, and resolving a positional clash between the hips joint and the spine's starting point so the rump cap lines up correctly.

Simplifying so the hips joint sits at the same location as the spine chain's start, keeping the bone influence list to just spine. Now I'm placing the loft stations along the body from the chest toward the tail, defining width and height at each cross-section to shape the belly sag and overall torso profile.

Checking chest depth against floor clearance and leg height to make sure the body sits believably above the legs. For coloring, I'm planning to use a countershaded paint (grey mottle fading to cream) with cel toon shading, and adding a furEdge paint along the belly transition to create a soft, jagged boundary between the dark back coloring and the cream underside.

Defining the color palette and darker saddle patch on the back using mottled noise between mid-grey and charcoal...

Now I'm thinking about adding fur card textures for chunky tufts scattered across the body, neck ruff, tail, and chest, referencing the reference image's texture.

I'll use full coat paint so each card gets lit/shadow based on its own normal. For the tuft shape, I'm drawing a pointed shard SVG path in white with a subtle grey stroke line down the center, sized up for clarity. Then I'm scattering around 220 cards across the body surface, filtering out the underside, with randomized size, lean, and bend to give a natural tufted look.

Now I'm working out the head structure — skull sphere, snout, and jaw as separate parts — and defining a clear local coordinate convention (forward/up/left) so I can place head features unambiguously without confusing world and model axes.

Still defining the snout shape...

Checking the overlap confirms a closed mouth, so I'll add a thin dark mouth-line rod along the snout for detail. For the eyes, I'm placing small amber spheres with black pupil spheres offset forward, plus a flatter dark eye-liner ellipsoid behind for depth.

Adding pale cream brow spots above each eye and giving the amber eyes a gentle glow for realism. For the ears, I'm extruding a triangular outline shape positioned at the top of the head.

Still working out the axis math...

Still working through the ear geometry math...

I'm sketching the ear outline points to form a rounded triangular shape with a sharp tip, keeping it mirror-symmetric, and deciding to skip extra details like dark rim shading or cheek ruff cards for now to keep things simple.

Instead I'll scatter cheek fur cards filtered to the upper cheek region, cream-colored and leaning back along the skull bone, then add a dark gradient brow stripe on the skull via painted texture. For the neck and chest I'm planning a thick sweep tapering from the base to the chin, plus a cream chest ruff sphere with downward-leaning tufted cards attached to the spine bone.

Now I'm working out the neck's path and overall height — checking that the joint positions give a believable withers and head height close to real wolf proportions (shoulder around 0.75-0.85m), and adjusting the neck endpoint downward since my current rig comes out a bit too tall.

I'm scaling the whole body down so the withers sit around 0.87 and the spine runs through a shallow curve from the hips forward, deciding this is stylized/heroic proportions so a bit of extra height is acceptable. I'm now laying out spine joint positions and figuring out which spine segment the front legs should parent to.

Continuing, I work out the neck and head chain, placing the neck joints rising from the spine toward the head joint, then extending the head forward to put the nose around z~1.0. Total body length comes to roughly 1.45 plus a 0.6 tail, which is long but fits a chunky heroic wolf, and head/ear height around 1.0-1.15 feels acceptably tall. Now I'm working out the body loft stations—width and height at each cross-section along the spine.

Checking the leg geometry: front leg root-to-target distance of 0.555 against segment lengths summing to 0.58 gives a slight bend, with the elbow aimed backward.

I'm narrowing the shoulder x-position slightly inward to keep legs from poking through the body surface. For the hind legs, the root-to-target distance of 0.58 versus a 0.72 segment sum produces a forward knee bend and backward hock, with the paw centered at ground level.

For the chain naming, the hind limb has four points giving three segments — hip, knee, hock, paw — labeled as a leg role. For the front limb I'm considering three points with two spans, named shoulder, elbow, wrist, though I'm weighing whether to add a third segment with matching bend directions so the wrist angles slightly forward like a real wolf's carpus.

Settling on three segments for both front and hind legs, with the last segment running parallel to the root-to-target line for a natural pose, and naming points shoulder/elbow/wrist/paw to match the hind leg's four-point convention. For leg thickness I'm tapering the sweep radii from thick at the top to thin at the paw, with the hind thigh bulging out more than the front shoulder, and defining a leg paint function that blends grey, dark, and cream tones based on vertical position and noise to create natural coat shading variation down each limb.

Now I'm adding detail to the paws and claws: darkening the shin area on the front edge of each leg for a stripe effect, then building cream-colored paw spheres with small conical claws (four per paw, three per claw set across all legs) attached at the paw joint, plus a few small cream toe bumps for texture.

I'm positioning the paw joints by referencing the end of each limb chain, aligning front and hind paw spheres with their respective foot targets, and making sure the hind leg's vertical cannon segment lines up naturally with the paw. Now I'm sketching out the tail chain path, starting from the hips and curving downward and backward through several waypoints toward the tip.

I'm working out the tail's segment names, radii that taper for a bushy look, and a coloring scheme that shades toward dark at the tip while keeping a creamy underside, using a paint function based on vertical position along the tail.

For fur cards, I'm setting scatter density and size along the tail surface with a downward-leaning flow direction to match how the tail hangs, then adjusting flow vectors separately for the body (angled back), neck (back-and-down), and ruff (outward lean).

For the coat texture, I'm using a cream tint for lighter tufts and a fur-edge cel shader with teeth and period parameters to create the mottled coat pattern, extending it to cover a cream chest bib.

Writing coat paint function...

Still tuning the coat zones...

Setting the palette values: mid grey, dark grey, cream, near-black claws, dark nose, and amber eyes.

Now I'm working out the head paint function, defining the head center in world space and shading the muzzle with a countershaded cream-over-grey cel effect.

Writing skull shading logic...

Setting the jaw colors and leaving the inside of the mouth for later. Now I'm working out the head joint's local coordinate frame, where offsets are specified in meters along the model's forward and up directions relative to that joint, independent of rotation.

I'm positioning the skull as an ellipsoid pushed forward and slightly wide for a chunky wolf head, checking it meets the neck radius smoothly, then sweeping the snout forward toward the nose tip with a tapering radius, and placing the eyes using forward/up/left offsets relative to the head frame.

I'm computing the ellipse equation at the eye's offset on the skull surface to find where the eye should sit relative to that curved boundary, then setting the eye sphere's radius and scale (flattened slightly in x) along with its liner.

Still placing eye details... adding pupil, glow, and brow dot, then starting the ear base position calculation relative to skull curvature.

Working out ear outline shape with convex points for the extruded ear geometry.

Skipping ear tufts for now, planning the neck ruff cards with cream/gray coat coloring and lean/flow parameters, then thinking through the dark mane on top and cream chest patches using scattered cards filtered by surface normal.

For the body I'm adding shoulder and haunch mass spheres bound to the spine and hips bones with coat coloring, then sketching out whiskers as thin dark rods extending from the muzzle outward and slightly back.

Now I'm switching whiskers to spike primitives (base to tip, tapered), six total across both sides, and planning a black lip line swept along the snout surface using points computed relative to the snout's tapering radius.

Next I'm positioning the jaw joint relative to the head bone and sketching its sweep path for the mouth opening.

Jaw joint sits at head.local forward 0.06, down 0.045, with the jaw bone sweeping between two rounded points. I'm adding cheek fluff as cream spheres plus cards for texture, then placing upper fang spikes at the head's forward 0.235 position pointing downward with small radius, and starting on the lower fangs attached to the jaw bone.

Lower fangs angle up into the snout cavity so the tips cross the upper fangs without poking through, and I check the geometry at each forward offset to confirm they stay tucked inside the mouth. I'm placing a black nose sphere at forward 0.3 with flattened scale, then considering a forehead fur tuft made of scattered cards along the skull surface.

Now I'm setting up rig roles for the skeleton—spine, neck, head, jaw, tail, legs—so skinning weights bind correctly, and starting the actual builder code with imports for path utilities, IK limb solving, paint/texture helpers, and toon/glow shading kits, then defining the metadata object for this Gray Wolf model before writing the main build function.

Defining color palette constants...

Writing coat shading logic...

Still writing paint logic...

Still writing leg shading logic...

Now I'm starting to build the actual wolf skeleton, defining the hips joint as the root and setting up a spine chain using catmull-rom curves through a series of 3D points.

Still writing joint hierarchy...

Still defining sweeps...

Adding neck scatter and chest tufts for the cream bib region, then starting the leg-building function with front limb placement parameters for both sides.

Defining limb joint names and chains...

Checking claw clearance against the floor, then moving to the hind paw geometry—mirroring the same paw-building function but positioned at the hip joint with its own sweep radii for the toe segments.

Now I'm adding fur card scatter for leg feathering near the elbows on the front legs, using filtered placement by height with cream-colored cards leaning outward, plus shoulder and haunch spheres built from a shared unit sphere geometry.

For the head, I'm setting up a local-coordinate helper to position parts relative to the skull, then placing the skull shape itself with its own scale and starting on a face-paint color function that'll shade it based on surface position.

Writing head paint logic...

Still defining muzzle, snout, and cheek geometry...

Now I'm scattering cards across the skull with a tint around "#6a6d74" for darker shading, filtering by normal direction, then setting up the eyes and whisker base positions per side.

Whiskers get spiked from base to tip with a light color on the head bone, then I move to the jaw joint setup, mouth line, fangs, ears, and a fur collar around the neck. I'm skipping the tongue since the mouth stays closed, and double-checking API signatures for part creation, joint binding, and sweep calls to avoid pitfalls.

Defining ear extrusion outline...

So the offset direction should move forward toward the front face, using the sign of the axis's z-component to determine which way local +z points. For the ear placement, the local y-axis naturally points upward, which works. I'm wrapping parts with glow effects and using plain amber color strings for the eyes rather than Paint objects, and building the teeth as spike cones running from a base point downward with small length and radius parameters.

I'm checking that the card texture function accepts Hit frames correctly, that the bone weighting works with the head bone, and that the scatter filter returns a boolean per hit to produce valid Hit arrays. I'm also verifying the limb function's signature for root, target, lengths, and bend directions, confirming the chain builder takes a path of Vector3 points with parent and naming options, and making sure the floor placement keeps the tail, paws, and claws properly grounded at the correct heights.

Toe spheres and the hind leg's rounded tip also sit correctly above the ground. I'm tallying up the total part count across the body, neck, tail, legs, paws, and head meshes to land around a hundred parts, then considering whether to add extra richness like collar claws, ear fur tufts, muscle definition, or a dark saddle stripe pattern.

I'm deciding most of these darker markings (spine stripe, leg stripes, tail tip, ear rim) can just be handled through paint/color rather than separate geometry, settling on a dark rim color for the outer ear with cream for the inner. Now I'm working through the rig details -- setting up the loft stations for the spine bone, positioning shoulder spheres relative to the spine joints, and confirming which utility imports (noise, smoothstep, mix, catmull, OutlinePoint, rng) are actually being used in the build.

I'm finalizing the leg paint colors and returning the root builder output, then double-checking types -- confirming color fields can accept either a string or Paint object, and typing the cheek parts array explicitly to avoid implicit any errors. I'm now writing out the jaw joint and jaw sweep code, picking a cream-based color for the jaw, and noticing the jaw tip's rounded cap would poke out slightly past the snout tip so I need to adjust the radius or position.

Checking that the extended measurement still fits within acceptable bounds -- it does, so I'm ready to write the final file.
